proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{2,\mathrm{loc}}\), \(n>4r\), \(i\in I_n\), and \(w\in\{1,2\}\).  Put \(A_i=\{i-r,\ldots,i+r\}\).  From the definitions of \(I_n\) and \(\Lambda_n\),
\[
 A_i\subseteq\Lambda_n. \tag{1}
\]
Write \(\Psi_i=(\Psi_i^E,\Psi_i^Y)\) for the Borel cylinder map supplied by the corrected locality condition.  Outside its one assignment-independent null event, simultaneously for every binary assignment \(d\),
\[
 E_i(d,G(U))
 =\Psi_i^E\bigl((U_{i+s})_{s=-r}^{r},(d_{i+s})_{s=-r}^{r}\bigr),
 \qquad
 Y_i(d;U,G(U))
 =\Psi_i^Y\bigl((U_{i+s})_{s=-r}^{r},(d_{i+s})_{s=-r}^{r}\bigr). \tag{2}
\]
The assignment-independent exceptional event in (2) is essential: (2) may be evaluated at the realized assignment without choosing a new conditional version.  Under the restriction coupling, the finite wave and the infinite wave have identical innovation and assignment coordinates on \(A_i\) by (1).  The graph edge-range condition also implies that the induced restriction removes no neighbor used at \(i\).  Therefore (2) gives equality of the finite- and infinite-volume exposure and realized-outcome coordinates.

It remains to verify equality of the propensity denominators rather than infer it from equality at one realized assignment.  Conditional on \(\mathcal F_U\), the local assignment vector has product \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\) law.  Hence, for \(a\in\{e_1,e_0\}\), both the finite and infinite conditional propensities equal
\[
 \sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^{\{-r,\ldots,r\}}}
 \mathbf 1\!\left\{
   \Psi_i^E\bigl((U_{i+s})_{s=-r}^{r},x\bigr)=a
 \right\}
 p^{\sum_s x_s}(1-p)^{2r+1-\sum_s x_s}. \tag{3}
\]
This finite sum is well defined because \(0<p<1\).  Exposure positivity makes each denominator in (3) at least \(\varepsilon>0\) almost surely.  Substitution of the equal exposure, outcome, and propensity coordinates into the two exposure-IPW formulas proves
\[
 Z_{n,i}^{(w)}=Z_i^{(w)}\qquad P\text{-almost surely}. \tag{4}
\]

Finally, \(\Lambda_n\setminus I_n\) contains precisely the \(r\) sites at each endpoint.  Thus, for fixed \(r\),
\[
 \frac{|\Lambda_n\setminus I_n|}{|\Lambda_n|}
 =\frac{2r}{n}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Equations (4) and the last display prove the proposition.

Fix \(n>4r\), \(\delta\in(0,1)\), and \(P\in\mathcal M_{2,\mathrm{loc}}\).  We first derive the common local score rule required by the already-established fixed-footprint F\o lner theorem.  Let \(A=\{-r,\ldots,r\}\), and write the site-zero cylinder map as \(\Psi_0=(\Psi_0^E,\Psi_0^Y)\).  For \(a\in\{e_1,e_0\}\) define the Borel function
\[
 \bar\pi_a(u_A)
 =\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^{A}}
   \mathbf 1\{\Psi_0^E(u_A,x)=a\}
   p^{\sum_{s\in A}x_s}(1-p)^{|A|-\sum_{s\in A}x_s}. \tag{1}
\]
The sum is finite, and the wavewise Bernoulli condition proves that (1) is the conditional exposure probability at the origin.  Define the raw Borel map
\[
 \widetilde z(u_A,x)=
 \Psi_0^Y(u_A,x)
 \left\{
  \frac{\mathbf 1\{\Psi_0^E(u_A,x)=e_1\}}{\bar\pi_{e_1}(u_A)}
  -\frac{\mathbf 1\{\Psi_0^E(u_A,x)=e_0\}}{\bar\pi_{e_0}(u_A)}
 \right\} \tag{2}
\]
when both denominators are positive, and set \(\widetilde z(u_A,x)=0\) otherwise.  Let
\[
 T_K(y)=\max\{-K,\min\{y,K\}\},
 \qquad z=T_K\circ\widetilde z. \tag{3}
\]
Then \(z\) is Borel and has codomain \([-K,K]\).

We next show that this one map represents every site.  Let \(\mathcal N\) be the common null set in the corrected cylinder condition.  The iid innovation law is stationary under the explicitly typed left shift, so
\[
 \mathcal N_\infty=\bigcup_{i\in\mathbb Z}\theta^{-i}\mathcal N
 \quad\text{satisfies}\quad P\{U\in\mathcal N_\infty\}=0. \tag{4}
\]
For \(U\notin\mathcal N_\infty\), apply the site-zero cylinder formula to \((\theta^iU,\theta^id)\).  Graph equivariance gives \(G(\theta^iU)=\theta^iG(U)\), while exposure and outcome equivariance, with their displayed orientation, give
\[
 \bigl(E_i(d,G(U)),Y_i(d;U,G(U))\bigr)
 =\Psi_0\bigl((U_{i+s})_{s\in A},(d_{i+s})_{s\in A}\bigr) \tag{5}
\]
for every \(i\) and every \(d\).  Applying the product Bernoulli kernel to (5) shows that \(\pi_i(a)=\bar\pi_a((U_{i+s})_{s\in A})\).  Thus \(\widetilde z\) evaluated at the realized local coordinates is exactly \(Z_i^{(w)}\).  The exact score-split lemma gives \(|Z_i^{(w)}|\le K\), so the truncation in (3) leaves that realized value unchanged.  Consequently, for both waves,
\[
 Z_i^{(w)}
 =z\bigl((U_{i+s})_{s\in A},(D_{i+s}^{(w)})_{s\in A}\bigr)
 \quad\text{almost surely for every }i\in\mathbb Z. \tag{6}
\]
Thus (2)--(6) derive, rather than assume, the single site- and wave-independent bounded score map required by \(\mathrm{thm{:}folner\text{-}fixed\text{-}footprint\text{-}two\text{-}wave\text{-}concentration}\).

Apply that theorem to the additive group \(\Gamma=\mathbb Z\), the footprint \(A\), and
\[
 C=AA^{-1}=A-A=\{-2r,\ldots,2r\}.
\]
The class assumptions provide iid innovations, the equivariant exposure and outcome rules, the conditional product \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\) law within each wave, and conditional independence across waves.  The common map premise is (6), with envelope (3).  For \(\Lambda=\Lambda_n\), the theorem's interior and pair sets are exactly \(I_n\) and \(J_{n,k}\).  Moreover,
\[
 |A|=2r+1,
 \qquad |C|=4r+1,
 \qquad N=N_n=n-2r,
 \qquad \nu=\min_{|k|\le2r}N_{n,k}=n-4r>0. \tag{7}
\]
The buffered-coupling proposition identifies the theorem's restricted scores with \(Z_{n,i}^{(w)}\), and the cross-wave-identification lemma identifies its covariance functional with \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}\).  Therefore its bias allowance is
\[
 \frac{4|C|^2K^2}{N}
 =\frac{4(4r+1)^2K^2}{N_n}=b_n, \tag{8}
\]
and its bounded-differences allowance is
\[
 \frac{\sqrt{48|\Lambda|}\,|A|\,|C|K^2}{\nu}
 \sqrt{\log(2/\delta)}
 =\frac{\sqrt{48n}(2r+1)(4r+1)K^2}{n-4r}
 \sqrt{\log(2/\delta)}
 =q_n(\delta). \tag{9}
\]
The established theorem now gives
\[
 P\!\left\{
  |\widehat\Omega_n^{12}-\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}|
  >b_n+q_n(\delta)
 \right\}\le\delta. \tag{10}
\]
The right side of (10), and the allowances (8)--(9), depend on the law only through the common class constants \(r,B,\varepsilon\).  Taking the supremum over \(P\in\mathcal M_{2,\mathrm{loc}}\) proves the asserted uniform inequality.

For an exact smallest-volume check, take \(r=1\), \(n=5\), the deterministic line graph, \(p=1/2\), \(E_i(d,G)=e_1\) for \(d_i=1\) and \(e_0\) for \(d_i=0\), and \(Y_i(d;U,G)=Bd_i\).  Then \(N_n=3\), \(Z_i^{(w)}=2BD_i^{(w)}\), \(m_i=B\), and \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}=0\).  For each of the \(2^{10}\) two-wave assignment arrays, every lag-product average and every product of wave means lies in \([0,4B^2]\), whence \(|\widehat\Omega_n^{12}|\le20B^2\).  Since \(\varepsilon<1/2\), \(K>2B\), and
\[
 b_n=\frac{100K^2}{3}>\frac{400B^2}{3}>20B^2.
\]
Thus no assignment rejects at this smallest admissible volume; direct averaging over all arrays gives \(\mathbb E_P\widehat\Omega_n^{12}=0\).  At the opposite boundary, (9) explicitly diverges as \(n\downarrow4r\); the root-\(n\) conclusion below therefore uses fixed \(r\) and does not assert a growing-range or Gaussian limit.

Let \(F_n=\widehat\Omega_n^{12}\).  The Janson boundary corollary gives \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}\ge0\), so the displayed null is the boundary of the one-sided alternative.  If \(P\in\mathcal M_{2,\mathrm{loc}}\) and \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}=0\), rejection implies
\[
 |F_n-\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}|=|F_n|
 >b_n+q_n(\alpha)=t_n(\alpha).
\]
The uniform concentration theorem at \(\delta=\alpha\) yields
\[
 P(\phi_{n,\alpha}=1)\le\alpha.
\]
Taking the supremum over the null class proves the size assertion.

Now suppose
\[
 \Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}ge\rho_n(\alpha,\beta)
 =2b_n+q_n(\alpha)+q_n(\beta). \tag{1}
\]
On nonrejection, \(F_n\le b_n+q_n(\alpha)\), and hence (1) gives
\[
 \Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}-F_n
 \ge b_n+q_n(\beta). \tag{2}
\]
For every \(\beta'\in(\beta,1)\), the map \(\delta\mapsto q_n(\delta)\) is strictly decreasing, because \(\log(2/\delta)\) is strictly decreasing.  Thus (2) implies
\[
 |F_n-\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}|>b_n+q_n(\beta').
\]
The concentration theorem at \(\delta=\beta'\) proves
\(P(\phi_{n,\alpha}=0)\le\beta'\).  Letting \(\beta'\downarrow\beta\) proves the non-strict boundary claim
\[
 P(\phi_{n,\alpha}=1)\ge1-\beta.
\]
This bound is uniform over every law satisfying (1), so taking the infimum proves the power assertion.

Finally, with \(r,B,\varepsilon,\alpha,\beta\) fixed, \(K=B/\varepsilon\) is fixed and \(N_n=n-2r\).  Hence
\[
 b_n=O(n^{-1}),
 \qquad
 q_n(\delta)
 =\frac{\sqrt{48n}(2r+1)(4r+1)K^2}{n-4r}
   \sqrt{\log(2/\delta)}
 =O(n^{-1/2})
\]
for each fixed \(\delta\in(0,1)\).  Substitution into (1) gives \(\rho_n(\alpha,\beta)=O(n^{-1/2})\).

We first prove the upper bound.  Exposure positivity makes every score coordinate a Borel function of one realized outcome, its exposure indicators, and its two known propensity coordinates.  Hence the definition of the canonical full observation supplies a law-independent Borel map \(T_n\) with
\[
 W_n=T_n(O_n^{\mathrm{obs}}). \tag{1}
\]
It follows that \(\widehat\Omega_n^{12}\), and therefore \(\phi_{n,\alpha}\), is a common Borel function of \(O_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\).  The size-and-separation theorem gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[\phi_{n,\alpha}]le\alpha
 \quad\text{when }\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_P[1-\phi_{n,\alpha}]le\beta
 \quad\text{when }\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}\ge\rho_n(\alpha,\beta), \tag{2}
\]
uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M_{2,\mathrm{loc}}\).  The defining optimization over \(\Phi_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\) therefore implies
\[
 s_{n,\alpha,\beta}^{\mathrm{obs}}le\rho_n(\alpha,\beta). \tag{3}
\]

For the converse, fix \(a\in(0,2B]\) and put \(b=a/2\), so \(0<b\le B\).  We construct a submodel inside the corrected class.  Take the deterministic nearest-neighbor line graph, iid \(U_i\sim\operatorname{Uniform}[0,1]\), and conditionally independent waves with iid \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) coordinates.  Because \(e_1\ne e_0\), define
\[
 E_i(d,G)=
 \begin{cases}
 e_1,&d_i=1,\\
 e_0,&d_i=0,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 C_i(d)=(d_i,d_{i+1})\in\mathcal C:=\{00,01,10,11\}. \tag{4}
\]
For \(v=(v_{00},v_{01},v_{10},v_{11})\in\{-b,b\}^4\), let
\[
 \mathcal H_0
 =\{v:v_{10}+v_{11}-v_{00}-v_{01}=0\}.
\]
This set has six elements.  Let \(Q_0\) be uniform on \(\mathcal H_0\), let
\[
 v^+=(-b,-b,b,b),
 \qquad v^-=-v^+,
\]
let \(Q_1=(\delta_{v^+}+\delta_{v^-})/2\), and define
\[
 Q_t=(1-t)Q_0+tQ_1,
 \qquad 0\le t<1. \tag{5}
\]
Enumerate the finite support of \(Q_t\), partition \([0,1]\) into consecutive half-open intervals having the corresponding \(Q_t\)-masses, and let \(F_t:[0,1]\to\{-b,b\}^4\) take the associated support value on each interval.  Then \(F_t\) is Borel and pushes the uniform law forward to \(Q_t\).  Put \(V_i=F_t(U_i)\), and use the same no-carryover schedule in both waves:
\[
 Y_i(d;U,G)=V_{i,C_i(d)}. \tag{6}
\]

We verify membership rather than treating (5)--(6) as if they implied it by definition.  The line graph is shift equivariant and has edge range one, which is at most \(r\) because \(r\) is a positive integer.  Equations (4) and (6) give
\[
 E_{i+k}(d,G)=E_i(\theta^kd,\theta^kG),
 \qquad
 Y_{i+k}(d;U,G)=Y_i(\theta^kd;\theta^kU,\theta^kG). \tag{7}
\]
More strongly, with no exceptional event at all, the single Borel map
\[
 \Psi_t((u_s)_{s=-r}^{r},(x_s)_{s=-r}^{r})
 =\begin{cases}
   \bigl(e_1,[F_t(u_0)]_{(x_0,x_1)}\bigr),&x_0=1,\\
   \bigl(e_0,[F_t(u_0)]_{(x_0,x_1)}\bigr),&x_0=0
  \end{cases} \tag{8}
\]
represents the exposure--outcome pair at every site after translating the local coordinates.  Thus (8) verifies the corrected joint assignment--innovation cylinder condition simultaneously for every assignment.  Also \(|Y_i|=b\le B\), and
\[
 \pi_i(e_1)=\pi_i(e_0)=\frac12>\varepsilon. \tag{9}
\]
Together with the iid innovations and the two Bernoulli waves, (7)--(9) verify every condition of \(\mathcal M_{2,\mathrm{loc}}\).  Denote the resulting law by \(P_t\).

Given \(V_i=v\), averaging over the four equiprobable cells in (4) and using the exposure-IPW definition gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 m_i
 &=\mathbb E_{P_t}\!\left[
 Y_i(D^{(w)};U,G)
 \left\{
  \frac{\mathbf 1\{D_i^{(w)}=1\}}{1/2}
  -\frac{\mathbf 1\{D_i^{(w)}=0\}}{1/2}
 \right\}
 \middle|\mathcal F_U\right]\\
 &=\frac{v_{10}+v_{11}-v_{00}-v_{01}}2.
\end{aligned}\tag{10}
\]
Thus \(m_i=0\) under every schedule in \(\mathcal H_0\), whereas it equals \(a\) at \(v^+\) and \(-a\) at \(v^-\).  Symmetry gives \(\tau_{\mathrm P}=0\).  Because the schedules are iid over sites, \((h_i)=(m_i)\) is iid, and therefore
\[
 \gamma_h(0)=a^2t,
 \qquad \gamma_h(k)=0\quad(k\ne0),
 \qquad \Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}(P_t)=a^2t. \tag{11}
\]
In particular, \(P_0\) is a null law.  Equation (10) proves that (11) changes the conditional causal exposure-effect score, rather than defining the target through an observed-law functional.

We now bound the information in the complete declared observation.  Conditional on both assignment arrays, site \(i\) reveals the ordered coordinate pair \((V_{i,c},V_{i,c'})\), where \(c=C_i(D^{(1)})\) and \(c'=C_i(D^{(2)})\).  Let \(R_j^{c,c'}\) be its law under \(Q_j\), for \(j\in\{0,1\}\), and order the atoms as \((b,b),(b,-b),(-b,b),(-b,-b)\).  Exhaustive enumeration of all six elements of \(\mathcal H_0\) and the two elements \(v^+,v^-\) gives
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\text{ordered cell pair}&R_0^{c,c'}&R_1^{c,c'}\\ \hline
c=c'&(1/2,0,0,1/2)&(1/2,0,0,1/2)\\
c\ne c'\text{ within one exposure group}
 &(1/6,1/3,1/3,1/6)&(1/2,0,0,1/2)\\
c,c'\text{ in opposite exposure groups}
 &(1/3,1/6,1/6,1/3)&(0,1/2,1/2,0).
\end{array} \tag{12}
\]
These rows cover all sixteen ordered pairs in \(\mathcal C^2\), providing the exact finite-cell stress test.  In every row, every atom charged by \(R_1^{c,c'}\) has positive \(R_0^{c,c'}\)-probability.  Hence the induced two-wave observed-outcome laws have common support even though the latent four-cell schedule laws need not.

Let \(R_t^{c,c'}=(1-t)R_0^{c,c'}+tR_1^{c,c'}\).  Direct substitution in (12) yields
\[
 \sum_x\frac{\{R_1^{c,c'}(x)-R_0^{c,c'}(x)\}^2}
 {R_0^{c,c'}(x)}
 =\begin{cases}0,&c=c',\\2,&c\ne c'.\end{cases} \tag{13}
\]
For probability masses \(R\ll S\), the elementary inequality \(\log u\le u-1\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(R\Vert S)
 \le\sum_x\frac{(R(x)-S(x))^2}{S(x)}. \tag{14}
\]
Applying (14) with (13) proves
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(R_t^{c,c'}\Vert R_0^{c,c'})\le2t^2. \tag{15}
\]

Conditional on the full assignments, the selected outcome pairs are independent over \(i\in I_n\), since each pair uses only \(V_i\).  The graph and assignment laws coincide under \(P_t\) and \(P_0\), while exposures and propensity coordinates are deterministic functions of them.  Conditional on the assignments, the Radon--Nikodym derivative of the outcome law is the product of the \(N_n\) sitewise derivatives.  Taking its logarithm, then its conditional expectation, turns that product into the following sum; averaging over the common assignment law and using (15) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\operatorname{KL}\!\left(
  \mathcal L_{P_t}(O_n^{\mathrm{obs}})
  \middle\Vert
  \mathcal L_{P_0}(O_n^{\mathrm{obs}})
 \right)\\
 &\quad=\mathbb E_D\sum_{i\in I_n}
 \operatorname{KL}\!\left(
  R_t^{C_i(D^{(1)}),C_i(D^{(2)})}
  \middle\Vert
  R_0^{C_i(D^{(1)}),C_i(D^{(2)})}
 \right)
 \le2N_nt^2.
\end{aligned}\tag{16}
\]
Thus (16) controls the complete declared record, not merely the score vector.

Put \(\eta=1-\alpha-\beta>0\) and
\[
 t_0=\frac{\eta}{\sqrt{2N_n}}.
\]
Since \(0<\eta<1\) and \(N_n\ge1\), \(0<t_0<1\), so \(P_{t_0}\) belongs to the submodel.  The cited Pinsker lemma and (16) imply
\[
 \operatorname{TV}\!\left(
  \mathcal L_{P_{t_0}}(O_n^{\mathrm{obs}}),
  \mathcal L_{P_0}(O_n^{\mathrm{obs}})
 \right)
 \le\sqrt{N_nt_0^2}=\frac{\eta}{\sqrt2}. \tag{17}
\]
Let \(\varphi_n\in\Phi_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\) have type-I error at most \(\alpha\) under every null law.  To cover randomized tests by the cited binary Le Cam lemma, adjoin under both laws the same independent \(A\sim\operatorname{Uniform}[0,1]\) and reject exactly when \(A\le\varphi_n(O_n^{\mathrm{obs}})\).  If \(\mu,\nu\) are the two laws of \(O_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\) and \(\lambda\) is the uniform law, then for every measurable \(H\), sectioning and integration give
\[
 |(\mu\times\lambda)(H)-(\nu\times\lambda)(H)|
 \le\int |\mu(H_u)-\nu(H_u)|\,d\lambda(u)
 \le\operatorname{TV}(\mu,\nu).
\]
The reverse inequality follows by taking \(H=C\times[0,1]\) and then the supremum over measurable \(C\).  Hence product with the common uniform law preserves total variation.  The Le Cam lemma and (17) yield
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_{t_0}}[1-\varphi_n(O_n^{\mathrm{obs}})]
 \ge1-\alpha-\frac{\eta}{\sqrt2}
 =\beta+\eta\left(1-\frac1{\sqrt2}\right)
 >\beta. \tag{18}
\]
By (11),
\[
 \Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}(P_{t_0})
 =\frac{a^2(1-\alpha-\beta)}{\sqrt{2N_n}}. \tag{19}
\]
For every proposed separation no larger than (19), the alternative set contains \(P_{t_0}\), while (18) rules out the required type-II guarantee for every test meeting the uniform null guarantee.  Taking the infimum in the definition of \(s_{n,\alpha,\beta}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) proves
\[
 s_{n,\alpha,\beta}^{\mathrm{obs}}
 \ge\frac{a^2(1-\alpha-\beta)}{\sqrt{2N_n}}. \tag{20}
\]
Combining (3) and (20), fixing any \(a\in(0,2B]\), using \(N_n=n-2r\), and using the proved bound \(\rho_n(\alpha,\beta)=O(n^{-1/2})\), establishes \(s_{n,\alpha,\beta}^{\mathrm{obs}}=\Theta(n^{-1/2})\).  Distinct labels are necessary for this witness: if \(e_1=e_0\), the two terms in every exposure-IPW score cancel identically.

By the canonical observation definition and exposure positivity, the law-independent Borel map \(T_n\) in
\[
 W_n=T_n(O_n^{\mathrm{obs}}) \tag{1}
\]
is well defined.  Thus every \(\psi_n\in\Psi_n\) induces the full-observation test \(\psi_n\circ T_n\in\Phi_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\), with exactly the same rejection probability under every \(P\in\mathcal M_{2,\mathrm{loc}}\).  The score tests are consequently a subclass of the full-observation tests.  Comparing the two defining feasible sets yields
\[
 s_{n,\alpha,\beta}^{\mathrm{score}}
 \ge s_{n,\alpha,\beta}^{\mathrm{obs}}. \tag{2}
\]
The full-observable minimax theorem therefore gives, for each \(0<a\le2B\),
\[
 s_{n,\alpha,\beta}^{\mathrm{score}}
 \ge\frac{a^2(1-\alpha-\beta)}{\sqrt{2N_n}}. \tag{3}
\]

For the upper bound, the full-observable minimax theorem certifies that the unchanged test \(\phi_{n,\alpha}\) has level at most \(\alpha\) and power at least \(1-\beta\) at separation \(\rho_n(\alpha,\beta)\).  Its displayed formula is a common Borel function of \(W_n\), so the same test is admissible in \(\Psi_n\).  The definition of the score radius gives
\[
 s_{n,\alpha,\beta}^{\mathrm{score}}
 \le\rho_n(\alpha,\beta). \tag{4}
\]
The already-established exactly unbiased lagged-statistic proposition separately shows that
\[
 \mathbf 1\{\widehat\Omega_n^{\mathrm u}>q_n^{\mathrm u}(\alpha)\}
\]
is a common Borel score-vector test with level at most \(\alpha\), power at least \(1-\beta\) whenever
\[
 \Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}
 \ge q_n^{\mathrm u}(\alpha)+q_n^{\mathrm u}(\beta),
\]
and no sample-centering bias allowance.  For fixed \(r,B,\varepsilon,\alpha,\beta\), this separation is \(O(n^{-1/2})\).  Finally, choose any fixed \(a\in(0,2B]\).  Since \(N_n=n-2r\), (3) is bounded below by a positive constant times \(n^{-1/2}\).  The displayed definition of \(\rho_n\), together with \(K=B/\varepsilon\), gives \(\rho_n(\alpha,\beta)=O(n^{-1/2})\), so (4) supplies the matching upper order.  Hence
\[
 s_{n,\alpha,\beta}^{\mathrm{score}}=\Theta(n^{-1/2}).
\]

proposed_core_edits.name: \(\theta\)

proposed.name: \(\theta\)
proposed.type: Left-shift actions on environments, assignments, and graphs
proposed.sig: For \(k\in\mathbb Z\), \(\theta^k\) acts on \(\mathcal U^{\mathbb Z}\), \(\{0,1\}^{\mathbb Z}\), and \(\mathcal G\).
proposed.def: For every \(k,j\in\mathbb Z\), \((\theta^ku)_j=u_{j+k}\) and \((\theta^kd)_j=d_{j+k}\); for every graph \(H\in\mathcal G\), \(\{i,j\}\in\theta^kH\) if and only if \(\{i+k,j+k\}\in H\).
proposed.role: Translation operator with a common left-shift orientation

proposed_core_edits.reason: The locality repair requires one explicitly typed shift action on environments, assignments, and graph edges so every equivariance identity has a fixed orientation.

proposed.condition:
There exist Borel maps
\[
 \Psi_i:\mathcal U^{\{-r,\ldots,r\}}\times
 \{0,1\}^{\{-r,\ldots,r\}}\longrightarrow\mathcal E\times\mathbb R,
 \qquad i\in\mathbb Z,
\]
and a Borel set \(\mathcal N\subseteq\mathcal U^{\mathbb Z}\) with \(P\{U\in\mathcal N\}=0\), where \(\mathcal N\) is independent of the assignment argument, such that for every \(u\notin\mathcal N\), every \(i\in\mathbb Z\), and every \(d\in\{0,1\}^{\mathbb Z}\),
\[
 \bigl(E_i(d,G(u)),Y_i(d;u,G(u))\bigr)
 =\Psi_i\bigl((u_{i+s})_{s=-r}^{r},(d_{i+s})_{s=-r}^{r}\bigr).
\]

standard.name: Exact bounded-neighborhood interference with common cylinder versions

proposed_core_edits.reason: Pointwise measurability for each assignment does not itself provide a version that can be evaluated simultaneously over all assignment cells.  The corrected cylinder condition supplies that common version without changing the locality radius or model scope.

proposed.name: Two-wave finite-range Palm exposure class
proposed.construction:
The class \(\mathcal M_{2,\mathrm{loc}}\) consists of the laws \(P\) such that: the coordinates \((U_i)_{i\in\mathbb Z}\) are iid; the graph satisfies
\[
 G(\theta^kU)=\theta^kG(U),
 \qquad N_G(i)\subseteq\{i-r,\ldots,i+r\};
\]
the exposure and outcome rules satisfy, for every \(i,k\in\mathbb Z\) and every assignment \(d\),
\[
 E_{i+k}(d,G)=E_i(\theta^kd,\theta^kG),
 \qquad
 Y_{i+k}(d;U,G)=Y_i(\theta^kd;\theta^kU,\theta^kG);
\]
there exist Borel maps
\[
 \Psi_i:\mathcal U^{\{-r,\ldots,r\}}\times
 \{0,1\}^{\{-r,\ldots,r\}}\longrightarrow\mathcal E\times\mathbb R,
 \qquad i\in\mathbb Z,
\]
and a single Borel set \(\mathcal N\subseteq\mathcal U^{\mathbb Z}\), with \(P\{U\in\mathcal N\}=0\) and independent of the assignment argument, such that for every \(u\notin\mathcal N\), every \(i\in\mathbb Z\), and every binary assignment \(d\),
\[
 \bigl(E_i(d,G(u)),Y_i(d;u,G(u))\bigr)
 =\Psi_i\bigl((u_{i+s})_{s=-r}^{r},(d_{i+s})_{s=-r}^{r}\bigr);
\]
the envelope \(|Y_i(d;U,G)|\le B\) holds almost surely for every \(i\) and \(d\); conditional on \(\mathcal F_U\), the coordinates of each \(D^{(w)}\), \(w\in\{1,2\}\), are iid \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\), and \(D^{(1)}\) and \(D^{(2)}\) are conditionally independent; and
\[
 \min_{a\in\{e_1,e_0\}}\pi_i(a)\ge\varepsilon
 \quad\text{almost surely for every }i\in\mathbb Z.
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: The class definition must contain the same joint assignment--innovation cylinder condition as its primitive locality assumption and must retain the corrected equivariance orientation.

prose_updates.tldr: Two conditionally independent assignment waves on one no-carryover schedule identify the Palm population covariance through observable cross-wave IPW products. A joint assignment--innovation cylinder version, common to every assignment outside one null set, makes the local conditional score well defined; on a Cayley graph the corresponding single site-independent Borel score map yields stationarity and bounded primitive influence. These primitives give order-\(n^{-1}\) centering bias and root-\(n\) finite-sample concentration on F\o lner interiors, with the buffered integer interval giving the explicit size--power test and an exactly unbiased lag-separated version. A four-cell exact-local least-favorable schedule gives common support to the induced laws of the complete buffered graph--assignment--exposure--outcome record and proves a matching full-observation minimax lower bound. Thus, for distinct focal exposure labels, both the full-observation and score-vector separation radii are \(\Theta(n^{-1/2})\) for fixed \(r,B,\varepsilon,\alpha,\beta\), \(p=1/2\), and \(\alpha+\beta<1\).

project_justification.gap: Janson2015 classifies the zero-long-run-variance boundary for finite block factors, and the one-wave interference papers study effect or estimator-variance inference. Viviano2020 already develops a two-wave network design in which a pilot estimates variance and the second wave optimizes participation and treatment; none of these works supplies a repeated-randomization test of the Palm population-covariance boundary or a full-observation minimax converse for it.
project_justification.niche: Conditional replication removes assignment noise from cross-wave IPW products. The joint assignment--innovation cylinder condition supplies one version simultaneously over all assignment cells; its Cayley-graph analogue is a single bounded Borel score rule shared by every site and wave. This common local rule derives stationarity and deterministic primitive influence on F\o lner interiors, while four local assignment cells leave unobserved schedule coordinates after two waves and give common support to the induced observed-data laws needed for a full-record information bound.
project_justification.fill: The project gives the cross-wave identity, order-\(n^{-1}\) centering control, root-\(n\) concentration, finite-sample size and power, and an exactly unbiased lag-separated interval statistic under the corrected common local versions. For distinct focal exposure labels, it also constructs a causal-realizable four-cell submodel with \(\operatorname{KL}\le2N_nt^2\) and linearly changing \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}\), proving matching \(\Theta(n^{-1/2})\) minimax rates for the complete declared observation and, as a corollary, for the score vector.

sampling_model.design: Two conditionally independent Bernoulli assignment waves with known probability \(p\) are applied to the same graph, exposure mapping, and no-carryover potential-outcome schedule after a prespecified washout; the deterministic covariance cutoff and analysis interior are fixed before assignment.
sampling_model.units: The canonical specialization observes \(\Lambda_n=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and analyzes its buffered interior \(I_n\). Exposure and outcome locality is a joint cylinder property: outside one law-null set independent of the assignment, one local Borel map represents every assignment cell. The group extension uses one site- and wave-independent Borel score map on a fixed right-translated footprint and deterministic F\o lner interiors of finitely generated amenable Cayley graphs.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary assignments in each wave generate local exposure labels and realized outcomes under one common shift-equivariant schedule; the left shift satisfies \((\theta^kd)_j=d_{j+k}\) and \(\{i,j\}\in\theta^kG\) if and only if \(\{i+k,j+k\}\in G\). The full minimax observation contains the finite graph, both assignments, both exposure arrays, both realized-outcome arrays, and known propensity coordinates.
sampling_model.overlap: Both focal exposures have conditional probability at least \(\varepsilon\) in each wave, so every IPW division is well defined.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Propensities are known from the design. The mean-centered statistic estimates only the two wave means, the lag-separated statistic removes that centering bias exactly, and neither procedure estimates unit-specific conditional scores or fits a regression.

prose_updates.related_work: Janson2015 supplies the finite-dependent coboundary result used to interpret the zero boundary, but no two-wave statistic or testing experiment. Leung2022ANI supplies one-wave exposure-IPW and approximate-neighborhood-interference analysis; no ANI or graph-HAC transfer is used here. AronowSamii2017 supplies exposure mappings and known design propensities. Viviano2020 is the closest design comparator: it uses a first-wave pilot to estimate variance and optimizes second-wave participation and treatment for average treatment and spillover effects. The present work does not claim that two-wave network designs are new; it instead uses conditionally independent replications with common joint local versions to identify and test a Palm covariance boundary and proves a full-observation common-support minimax converse. LiWager2022 and FanLengWu2025 target causal-effect estimation and estimator variance under graphon models. Tsybakov2009 supplies the classical Pinsker and two-point testing inequalities used after the new four-cell likelihood calculation.
prose_updates.interpretation: The null \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}=0\) is a covariance-cancellation boundary, not a claim that conditional exposure effects are homogeneous. On the line, the corrected joint cylinder condition makes the conditional score a finite block factor, so Janson's result represents the null score as a finite-block coboundary. Rejection certifies positive Palm population variation; failure to reject only places that variation within the stated finite-sample threshold.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The design requires two conditionally independent assignment waves applied to one no-carryover schedule and one common joint assignment--innovation cylinder version. The full-observation converse includes the observed finite graph, assignments, exposures, realized outcomes, and known propensities, but not the innovations or unobserved assignment-cell outcomes. The graph extension requires a single bounded local score map shared by all sites and waves, a fixed footprint, and deterministic covariance-support sets on F\o lner interiors. No growing bandwidth, random shortest-path cutoff, approximate-neighborhood-interference transfer, endogenous graph-distance HAC, annealed CLT or Wald theorem, or BondEtAl2012 reanalysis is claimed.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The causal target is \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}\), the long-run covariance sum of fixed local conditional exposure-effect scores under the Palm law. The interval results and their finitely generated amenable Cayley-graph extension use a fixed deterministic local cutoff, bounded outcomes, overlap, two conditionally independent waves, a common assignment--innovation cylinder version, bounded primitive influence, bounded score dependency, and a common Palm mean. In the group extension, one site- and wave-independent Borel score rule is derived from the cylinder condition and equivariance. For distinct focal exposure labels, minimax sharpness holds for the explicitly encoded finite observed-data vector at \(p=1/2\) and \(\alpha+\beta<1\); the score-vector theorem is a corollary. The note claims neither novelty of two-wave designs nor validity for richer observations that reveal innovations or unobserved potential outcomes.

statement_notes.justification: The exact interior coupling is now derived from one assignment-independent local cylinder version, so evaluating the rule at a realized wave cannot change conditional versions.
statement_notes.gap: BaryshnikovYukich2005 studies stabilizing finite-volume scores, while this proposition records exact boundary deletion for two repeated exposure experiments under a common local version.
statement_notes.consumer: An experimenter can implement the diagnostic after dropping a prespecified fixed-width endpoint buffer.

statement_notes.justification: The corrected cylinder condition and shift equivariance derive the single bounded local score map used by the explicit uniform deviation inequality.
statement_notes.gap: Janson2015 classifies zero long-run variance but supplies no test from randomized causal scores; FanLengWu2025 estimates an asymptotic estimator variance under a low-rank graphon model and does not give this two-wave finite-sample bound.
statement_notes.consumer: Repeated experiments obtain a prespecified, regression-free error bar for the population component even at the degenerate coboundary boundary.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem turns the uniform concentration map into a nonasymptotic level guarantee and an explicit root-sample-size power separation.
statement_notes.gap: Leung2022ANI gives one-assignment network-HAC inference, and FanLengWu2025 gives graphon-based variance inference; neither tests a Palm exposure-score covariance by repeated assignments.
statement_notes.consumer: A platform with two washout-separated waves can test whether the Palm population component is detectably positive.

statement_notes.justification: A causal-realizable four-cell schedule verifies corrected class membership and gives a common-support likelihood bound for every Borel test of the complete declared record.
statement_notes.gap: Viviano2020 optimizes a second-wave design after a pilot; it does not prove a full-observation information lower bound for testing the Palm covariance boundary.
statement_notes.consumer: A designer can use the finite-sample upper threshold knowing that no common Borel test of the declared full observation improves its separation order uniformly over the class.

statement_notes.justification: The score-vector result follows by the Borel reduction from the full record and retains both the mean-centered and exactly unbiased operational tests.
statement_notes.gap: A score-only likelihood calculation would not control procedures that inspect raw outcomes; the full-record four-cell comparison closes that gap before restriction to scores.
statement_notes.consumer: Implementations retaining only the two IPW score arrays inherit the same sharp root-sample-size separation rate.
